Abstract: Developing scalable and generalizable reward engineering for reinforcement learning (RL) is crucial for creating general-purpose agents, especially in the challenging domain of robotic manipulation. This article introduces text-to-video reward (TeViR), a novel method that leverages a pretrained text-to-video diffusion model to generate dense rewards by comparing the predicted image sequence with current observations. Abstract: The rapid advancement of generative AI highlights the importance of text-to-image security, particularly with the threat of backdoor poisoning. Timely disclosure and mitigation of security vulnerabilities in text-to-image diffusion models are crucial for ensuring the safe deployment of generative models. We explore a novel training-free backdoor poisoning paradigm through model editing, which is recently employed for knowledge updating in large language models. Nevertheless, we reveal the potential security risks posed by model editing techniques to image generation models. In this work, we establish the goals for backdoor attacks based on model editing, and propose a relationship-driven precise backdoor poisoning method, REDEditing. Drawing on the goals of equivalent-attribute alignment and stealthy poisoning, we develop an equivalent relationship retrieval and joint-attribute transfer approach that ensures consistent backdoor image generation through concept rebinding. A knowledge isolation constraint is proposed to preserve clean generation integrity. Compared to state-of-the-art approaches, our method achieves an 11% higher attack success rate and a 24% improvement in backdoor stealthiness, while also yielding more natural outputs. This work aims to heighten awareness regarding this security vulnerability in editable image generation models.

Abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) are state-of-the-art architectures for various vision tasks. Deploying DiTs on GPUs often incurs significant memory overhead and inference latency that can be alleviated via quantization. However, designing an efficient quantization system for DiTs is highly challenging because their iterative denoising pipeline reuses quantized weights, amplifying rounding errors far more than in large language models and forcing a tight balance between storage savings and generative fidelity, which can be sharpened by three findings: (1) activation quantization causes drastic quality degradation, so practical deployments must adopt weight-only schemes while keeping accuracy loss minimal; (2) the resolution-dependent sweet spot in precision often lands on non-power-of-two bit-widths; and (3) such irregular precisions misalign GPU memory transactions and trigger warp-level bank conflicts that throttle efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose QDiTx, an innovative framework that enables efficient quantization of DiT models for arbitrary bit-widths. Its offline stage performs resolution-aware precision search and cascaded quantization to preserve fidelity with compact metadata, while its online stage deploys warp-aware weight allocation and overlapped dequantization/inference pipelines to sustain SIMT efficiency. We integrate QDiTx into the inference pipeline of existing DiT models. Evaluation results demonstrate that QDiTx reduces the inference time by up to 7× in weight-loading-dominated workloads while preserving generation quality, with at most a 6.7% FID increase in the reported DiT-XL/2 settings compared to the FP32 baseline.

Abstract: Facing the rapid development of both user equipment (UE) and mobile applications, mobile edge computing (MEC) emerged as a new paradigm to furnish UE with satisfactory computational capability and task latency. Studies on MEC have put a great deal of focus on computation offloading, mainly involving multi-step task offloading and resource allocation (OffAll) which is mostly non-trivial. Concerning the heavy burden of online OffAll optimization on scalability and efficiency, offline learning-based OffAll approaches are of high popularity. However, most existing learning-based OffAll is still short of generalizability and adaptability across different MECs, thus difficult for general-purpose application. Inspired by the remarkable success of LLMs for their impressive generalization ability across different tasks by conditioning on instructions or prompts, this paper proposes a diffusion-based OffAll approach (termed DiffLoader) by utilizing the generative conditional-planning ability of diffusion models learned from multi-MEC OffAll experiences. Specifically, we leverage a few-shot trajectory of MEC states transitions as MEC-specific prompts, adopt diffusion to learn multi-MEC conditional OffAll distribution, and generate OffAll decisions via distribution-sampling during execution. We conduct extensive experiments to verify the advantages of DiffLoader over state-of-the-art learning-based multi-MEC OffAll approaches, and also show the compositive generating ability of DiffLoader even for unseen MEC.

Abstract: The 6G wireless communications aim to establish an intelligent world of ubiquitous connectivity, providing an unprecedented communication experience. Large artificial intelligence models (LAMs) are characterized by significantly larger scales (e.g., billions or trillions of parameters) compared to typical artificial intelligence (AI) models. LAMs exhibit outstanding cognitive abilities, including strong generalization capabilities for fine-tuning to downstream tasks, and emergent capabilities to handle tasks unseen during training. Therefore, LAMs efficiently provide AI services for diverse communication applications, making them crucial tools for addressing complex challenges in future wireless communication systems. This study provides a comprehensive review of the foundations, applications, and challenges of LAMs in communication. First, we introduce the current state of AI-based communication systems, emphasizing the motivation behind integrating LAMs into communications and summarizing the key contributions. We then present an overview of the essential concepts of LAMs in communication. This includes an introduction to the main architectures of LAMs, such as transformer, diffusion models, and mamba. We also explore the classification of LAMs, including large language models (LLMs), large vision models (LVMs), large multimodal models (LMMs), and world models, and examine their potential applications in communication. Additionally, we cover the training methods and evaluation techniques for LAMs in communication systems. Lastly, we introduce optimization strategies such as chain of thought (CoT), retrieval augmented generation (RAG), and agentic systems. Following this, we discuss the research advancements of LAMs across various communication scenarios, including physical layer design, resource allocation and optimization, network design and management, edge intelligence, semantic communication, agentic systems, and emerging applications. Finally, we analyze the major challenges in current research, including the lack of high-quality and structured communication data, hallucination and limited reasoning in generative models, poor explainability and adaptability, deployment under resource constraints, as well as security and privacy risks, and provide insights into potential future directions.

Abstract: Social media platforms have emerged as critical arenas for the formation and evolution of public opinion, where emotional expressions frequently dictate the direction and intensity of online discussions. Although previous studies have highlighted the role of emotions in information diffusion, limited attention has been given to how heterogeneous user groups participate in emotional dynamics across different stages of public opinion development. To address this gap, this study proposes a machine learning–based analytical framework that combines user label identification with sentiment analysis to investigate emotional dynamics in social media discussions. Using large-scale Weibo data related to the impeachment controversy surrounding South Korean President Yoon Suk-yeol, personality-oriented expression labels are identified from textual and profile features, and their corresponding emotional trajectories are analyzed across the public opinion life cycle. The results demonstrate clear stage-based differences in how distinct user groups participate in emotional discourse, revealing an asymmetric pattern of participation over time. In the initial stage, users exhibiting more introspective and emotionally responsive expression styles appear earlier and contribute a substantial proportion of early emotional reactions, facilitating the issue’s capacity to gain public attention. During the diffusion stage, users with outward-oriented and interpretive expression styles become increasingly active, coinciding with stronger emotional polarization and accelerated information circulation. In the later stages, analytically oriented expression styles become more prominent, and emotional intensity gradually declines as discussions shift toward reflective engagement. Overall, these findings indicate that emotional dynamics in social media public opinion are shaped by asymmetric participation patterns among heterogeneous user groups, offering a data-driven perspective for understanding how diverse expression tendencies influence the temporal evolution of online discussions.
